title: Local-to-global necessity unproved: need 'each off-diag cell is ordinary-column in some mode' + honest punctured reconstruction

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**The local-to-global necessity step is not proved; Lemma `offrank1` (a)=>(b) relies on the false "no-missing-entries" reduction.**

What actually makes the certificate $\mathbf F$ correct (empirically verified: $200$ random off-diagonal perturbations of products all caught; products give all-mode rank exactly $4$) is the structural fact:

> **(*)** Every off-diagonal cell $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$ is an *ordinary-column* cell in at least one of the four modes.
> (Its complementary triple is all-equal in all four modes simultaneously only if $\alpha=\beta=\gamma=\delta$.)

Hence if $\lambda$ is non-product, then $\operatorname{rank}\Lambda'^{(m)}\ge2$ for **some** mode $m$, and *that* mode's $5\times5$-minor certificate fires. (Concretely, the q9-12 counterexample is non-product and is caught in modes $2,3,4$, which have rank $15$.)

The current proof does **not** establish (*) or the resulting local-to-global implication. Instead, Lemma `offrank1` (a)$\Rightarrow$(b) asserts eq:Lamrank1 ("rank $\Lambda'^{(m)}\le1$ in all modes") is the same as $r_m^{\mathrm{off}}\le1$ and then claims $\Lambda'$ "has no missing entries so the classical $2\times2$-minor fact applies." Both claims are wrong (q9-12): $\Lambda'$ is missing the $n(n-1)$ cells $(\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta)$.

**Required correct necessity argument.**
1. From $\operatorname{rank}\mathbf S_{(m)}\le4\ \forall m$ deduce $\operatorname{rank}\Lambda'^{(m)}\le1\ \forall m$ (corrected Thm `lower`, q9-14).
2. Prove (*) and use it to cover **every** off-diagonal cell — including the $(\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta)$ cells — by a single-mode separation in a mode where its column triple is ordinary.
3. Run the telescoping reconstruction $\lambda_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}=u_\alpha v_\beta w_\gamma x_\delta$ honestly across all four modes, proving consistency (the printed telescoping *formula* is correct for genuine products, verified numerically to $10^{-16}$; what is missing is the *derivation* that all-mode rank-$\le1$ forces it on the punctured support).

A clean way to do step 2-3: show the off-diagonal $2\times2$ box minors (over the union of all four modes' ordinary boxes) already imply rank-one of the full off-diagonal array. A tangent-space check at a product point gives solution-variety dimension exactly $4n-3$ (= product family dimension), supporting this; it now needs a genuine (not merely tangential / generic) proof.
